[[Alexander Zverev]] defeated [[Ben Shelton]] in the final, 6–3, 7–6<sup>(7–2)</sup>, 5–7, 6–2 to win the men's singles tennis title at the [[2026 US Open (tennis)|2026 US Open]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/zverev-shelton-us-open-2026-final-report|title=Zverev doubles up in 2026, stymies Shelton for US Open title|website=atptour.com|publisher=[[ATP Tour]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260914052755/https://www.atptour.com/en/news/zverev-shelton-us-open-2026-final-report|url-status=live|archive-date=14 September 2026}}</ref>
It was his second [[Grand Slam (tennis)#Tournaments|major]] title, following the [[2026 French Open – Men's singles|2026 French Open]]. Zverev was the fourth man in the [[Open Era]] to win his first two majors in the same year (after [[Jimmy Connors]] in [[1974 Grand Prix (tennis)|1974]], [[Guillermo Vilas]] in [[1977 Grand Prix (tennis)|1977]], and [[Jannik Sinner]] in [[2024 ATP Tour|2024]]), and the first German man to win the [[US Open (tennis)|US Open]] since [[Boris Becker]] in [[1989 US Open – Men's singles|1989]].<ref name="sascha">{{cite web|url=https://www.tennismajors.com/roland-garros-news/zverev-makes-it-two-majors-in-a-year-and-only-alcaraz-and-sinner-beat-him-at-one-on-the-big-stage-in-2026-860952.html|title=Zverev Wins Second Major of Year at US Open 2026|author=Cédric Rouquette|date=14 September 2026|website=tennismajors.com|publisher=Tennis Majors|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260914041747/https://www.tennismajors.com/roland-garros-news/zverev-makes-it-two-majors-in-a-year-and-only-alcaraz-and-sinner-beat-him-at-one-on-the-big-stage-in-2026-860952.html|url-status=live|archive-date=14 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/tennis/story/_/id/49933388/alexander-zverev-beats-ben-shelton-4-sets-win-2026-us-open|title=Alexander Zverev beats Ben Shelton in 4 sets to win US Open|website=espn.com|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=13 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260913231736/https://www.espn.com/tennis/story/_/id/49933388/alexander-zverev-beats-ben-shelton-4-sets-win-2026-us-open|url-status=live|archive-date=13 September 2026}}</ref> 

[[Carlos Alcaraz]] was the defending champion, but lost in the quarterfinals to Shelton. Their quarterfinal match marked the latest finish in tournament history, at 3:33 a.m.,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/tennis/story/_/id/49877286/ben-shelton-stuns-carlos-alcaraz-5-set-late-night-epic-make-us-open-semifinals|title=Ben Shelton stuns Carlos Alcaraz in late-night US Open marathon|date=9 September 2026|work=ESPN|accessdate=9 September 2026}}</ref> surpassing the previous record from the [[2022 US Open – Men's singles|2022]] quarterfinal between Alcaraz and Sinner.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/articles/c20v6pgz7nmo|title=Shelton beats Alcaraz in late-night 'war' to reach semis|date=8 September 2026|work=BBC News|accessdate=9 September 2026}}</ref>

[[Novak Djokovic]]'s first-round defeat to [[Mariano Navone]] marked only his third career loss in the opening round of a major, his first opening-round loss at the US Open, and his earliest loss at a major since the [[2006 Australian Open – Men's singles|2006 Australian Open]].<ref>{{Cite web| title=Mariano Navone stuns physically ailing Novak Djokovic at US Open|publisher=ATPTour|date=31 August 2026|url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/djokovic-navone-us-open-2026-r1|accessdate=31 August 2026}}</ref> This marked the first time that none of the [[Big Three (tennis)#Grand Slam events|Big Three]] reached the second round of a major since the [[2003 French Open – Men's singles|2003 French Open]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Novak Djokovic's US Open exit ends remarkable Big Three Grand Slam streak|publisher=Sportstar|date=31 August 2026|url =https://sportstar.thehindu.com/tennis/novak-djokovic-us-open-exit-big-three-streak-2003-french-open/article71409707.ece |accessdate=31 August 2026}}</ref> As a result of his loss, Djokovic dropped out of the top 10 in the ATP rankings for the first time since July 2018, marking the first time since October 2002 in which none of the Big Three were ranked in the top 10.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/articles/ckgvrdz061eo|title=Djokovic's tearful loss leaves future uncertain|accessdate=2 September 2026|date=1 September 2026|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref>

[[Arthur Géa]] was the first [[Glossary of tennis terms#Lucky loser|lucky loser]] to reach the fourth round since [[Corentin Moutet]] in [[2022 US Open – Men's singles|2022]], and the second to do so in the [[Open Era]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.usopen.org/en_US/news/articles/2026-09-05/lucky_loser_arthur_gea_beats_michael_zheng_to_reach_2026_us_open_fourth_round.html |title= Lucky loser Arthur Gea beats Michael Zheng to reach 2026 US Open fourth round |website=usopen.org}}</ref>
With his win over 12th seed [[Rafael Jódar]], [[Bu Yunchaokete]] became the first lucky loser to defeat a top 15 seed in the first round of the US Open in the Open Era.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/bu-jodar-us-open-2026-wednesday|title= Buyunchaokete dispatches Jodar, who won just 4 games in US Open defeat| website=ATPTour |date=2 September 2026}}</ref><ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/tennis/story/_/id/49797267/us-open-2026-lucky-losers-casper-ruud-vendula-valdmannova |title= The uncertain days of a potential lucky loser at the US Open|website=[[ESPN]]|date=2 September 2026}}</ref><ref> {{cite web|url= https://clutchpoints.com/tennis/us-open-news-bu-yunchaokete-open-era-history-lucky-loser-win-rafael-jodar |title= Bu Yunchaokete makes U.S. Open history with shocking win over Rafael Jodar as lucky loser |website= ClutchPoints.com |date=2 September 2026|accessdate=4 September 2026}}</ref>

This tournament marked the first absence from a major of [[List of ATP number 1 ranked singles players|world No. 1]] Sinner, since making his major debut at the [[2019 US Open – Men's singles|2019 US Open]]. It was the first time the reigning world No. 1 did not participate at the US Open.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/sinner-us-open-2026-withdrawal|title=Jannik Sinner withdraws from the US Open|date=August 21, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260822074630/https://www.atptour.com/en/news/sinner-us-open-2026-withdrawal|url-status=live|archive-date=August 22, 2026}}</ref>

This tournament marked the final major appearance of [[2016 US Open – Men's singles|2016]] champion, three-time major champion and former world No. 3 [[Stan Wawrinka]], and the final professional appearance of former world No. 6 [[Gaël Monfils]].<ref>{{cite web |title= Wawrinka given late wildcard for US Open farewell |url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/articles/cvgye2w5x20o |website=BBC Sport |accessdate=26 August 2026 |date=26 August 2026}}</ref> Wawrinka lost in the first round to [[Matteo Berrettini]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usopen.org/en_US/news/articles/2026-08-31/stan_wawrinka_thrills_2026_us_open_crowd_in_final_grand_slam_match.html|title= Stan Wawrinka thrills 2026 US Open crowd in final Grand Slam match|date=31 August 2026}}</ref> while Monfils lost in the second round to [[Learner Tien]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/monfils-us-open-2026-farewell|title= Monfils receives hero’s farewell, Grand Slam career ends in New York| website=ATPTour |date=4 September 2026}}</ref>
